sys_atf_step.notes: Finds and validates the Reservation Tracker record dynamically. Uses a custom server script because the native UI Record Query cannot match a text RITM number string with the Sys ID data pill. Evaluates the record state against Parameters.u_expected_approval to seamlessly support both Approval and Rejection execution pathways.

(function(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual) {
    var step6 = 'a72db2ae831ec7101902ba96feaad35c';
    var scReqItemTbl = 'sc_req_item';

    // 1. Get the RITM Sys ID that was opened in your test session
    // (Ensure this matches your actual step that opens or queries the form)
    var ritmSysId = steps(step6).first_record;

    // 2. Read the dynamic UI Action name from your parameter data set
    var actionToClick = params.u_expected_approval; // "Approve" or "Reject"

    var gr = new GlideRecord(scReqItemTbl);
    if (gr.get(ritmSysId)) {

        // 3. This triggers the business rules/flows tied to that specific button action
        // It uses the backend action name (usually lower-case match like 'approve' or 'reject')
        var actionName = actionToClick.toLowerCase();

        // Execute the UI action logic on the server record container
        // var actionSuccess = gs.executeAction(actionName, gr);

		// 4. Use ServiceNow's native UIActionUtils API to execute the button logic
        var uiActionUtils = new SNC.UIActionUtils();
        uiActionUtils.executeUIAction(actionName, gr);

        stepResult.setOutputMessage('Successfully clicked dynamic action: ' + actionToClick);
        stepResult.setSuccess();
    } else {
        stepResult.setOutputMessage('Failed to find open RITM record to click action.');
        stepResult.setFailed();
    }
})(outputs, steps, params, stepResult, assertEqual);
